entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Metrophanes of Byzantium was the 26th bishop of Byzantium, serving from approximately 306 to 314 CE. He is the first bishop mentioned by contemporary sources and is considered the foundation of the organized Christian community in Byzantium. Metrophanes played a crucial role in the early development of Christianity in the region, and his legacy continued to shape the city's religious landscape for centuries to come.

As bishop, Metrophanes oversaw the establishment of several churches and monasteries, including the famous Church of St. John the Baptist. He also played a key role in the translation of the Bible into the local language, which helped to spread Christianity throughout the region.

Metrophanes' significance extends beyond his immediate role as bishop, as he represents the early adoption of Christianity in the Byzantine Empire. His commitment to the faith helped to pave the way for the spread of Christianity throughout the Mediterranean world.

In the centuries following his death, Metrophanes was revered as a saint by the Orthodox Church, and his feast day is still celebrated in Byzantium today.

Metrophanes of Byzantium's legacy is a testament to the enduring power of Christianity in the ancient world. His contributions to the development of the faith in Byzantium continue to inspire and educate historians and scholars today.
